title: CHAPTER 4: POLITY AND GOVERNANCE OF HIMACHAL PRADESH

cells: Unicameral (single house: Vidhan Sabha only; no Vidhan Parishad)
68 elected + provision for 1 nominated Anglo-Indian (if needed under older law); effective 68
Senior-most member sworn as Protem Speaker during new assembly
5 years (can be dissolved earlier by Governor on CM's advice)

blocks.content: 4.2 Governor, CM and Council of Ministers

cells: Dr. Yashwant Singh Parmar (1952); called 'Father of Himachal Pradesh'
CM + Cabinet Ministers + MoS; bound by collective responsibility
Shimla (also winter capital functions from Shimla; Dharamshala is second capital)

items: HP High Court established 25 January 1971, the day HP became a full state; located in Shimla.
First Chief Justice of HP High Court: Justice M.H. Beg.
District courts are at all 12 district headquarters.
HP Lokayukta: Quasi-judicial body to investigate corruption complaints against public servants.
HP Information Commission (under RTI Act): Shimla.
HP State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission: Shimla.
HP Police Act 2007: Governs the HP Police; replaced the older colonial Police Act 1861.
HP Public Service Commission (HPPSC): Conducts HP Administrative Service and allied examinations.
HP Staff Selection Commission (HPSSC): Conducts Group C and D recruitment examinations.
Governed by HP Panchayati Raj Act 1994 implementing 73rd Constitutional Amendment.
Three tiers: Gram Panchayat (village) → Panchayat Samiti (block) → Zila Parishad (district).
Women's reservation: 50% in Panchayati Raj Institutions in HP.
Urban Local Bodies: 2 Municipal Corporations (Shimla, Dharamshala), 29 Municipal Councils, 22 Nagar Panchayats.
Shimla Municipal Corporation is the highest urban local body.
HP State Election Commission conducts Panchayat and Municipality elections.
